title: Initial equation and tangent cone of a regular local hypersurface
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a regular local ring of dimension $d$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], where $k=A/\mathfrak m$, and let $0\ne f\in\mathfrak m$. Put $B=A/(f)$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m B$. For associated graded rings [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], there is a unique finite integer $e\ge1$ with $f\in\mathfrak m^e\setminus\mathfrak m^{e+1}$. Write $F$ for the class of $f$ in the degree-$e$ part of $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A$. For any minimal generators $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ of $\mathfrak m$, the canonical maps induce graded $k$-algebra isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A\cong k[Z_1,\ldots,Z_d],\qquad
\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}B\cong (\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A)/(F),$$
where $Z_i$ maps to the class of $a_i$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Moreover $\dim B=d-1$, and the dimension of the vector space $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$ over $k$ is $d-1$ if $e=1$ and $d$ if $e\ge2$. Consequently $B$ is regular local if and only if $f\notin\mathfrak m^2$.

proof.text: Fix any minimal generators $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ of $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] they form an $A$-regular sequence. Apply [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial] with $R=A$, $c=d$, $J=\mathfrak m$ and $B=k$. Its displayed map is exactly $Z_i\mapsto[a_i]_1$, and gives the first asserted graded $k$-algebra isomorphism. In particular the classes $[a_i]_1$ are a $k$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] to $R=M=A$ and $I=\mathfrak m$: $A$ is Noetherian by regularity, $A$ is generated by $1$ as an $A$-module, and the Jacobson radical of a local ring is its unique maximal ideal. Hence $\bigcap_{q\ge0}\mathfrak m^q=0$. For each $0\ne x\in A$ choose the least $q$ with $x\notin\mathfrak m^q$; it is positive, and $v(x)=q-1$ is the unique integer with $x\in\mathfrak m^{v(x)}\setminus\mathfrak m^{v(x)+1}$. Taking $x=f$ gives $e=v(f)\ge1$ and the nonzero homogeneous class $F=[f]_e$.

Put $G=\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A$. The polynomial ring of step 1 has no zero divisors: order monomials lexicographically; in a product of two finite nonzero polynomials the largest monomial is the product of their largest monomials, with nonzero coefficient in the field $k$. Thus, for $x,y
e0$, their nonzero initial classes have nonzero product in $G$. By the multiplication formula of [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], this product is the class of $xy$ in degree $v(x)+v(y)$, so $xy
otin\mathfrak m^{v(x)+v(y)+1}$, $xy
e0$ and $v(xy)=v(x)+v(y)$. In particular $v(af)=v(a)+e$ for $a
e0$.

proof.text: The quotient map $\pi:A\to B$ sends $\mathfrak m^q$ onto $\mathfrak n^q$: each product of $q$ images lifts to a product, and sums lift termwise. Thus the degreewise quotient maps give a surjective graded $k$-algebra map $\phi:G\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}B$ using [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. A homogeneous class $[x]_q$ is in its kernel exactly when $x=y+af$ with $y\in\mathfrak m^{q+1}$. Then $af\in\mathfrak m^q$. If $a\ne0$, step 3 gives $v(a)+e\ge q$. For $q<e$ this forces $af\in\mathfrak m^{q+1}$ and the class is zero. For $q\ge e$, it gives $a\in\mathfrak m^{q-e}$ (also true for $a=0$), and $[x]_q=[af]_q=F[a]_{q-e}$. Conversely every such product maps to zero because $\pi(f)=0$. Consequently $\ker(\phi)_q=F G_{q-e}$ for $q\ge e$, and is zero for $q<e$.

source.place: Tag 00NO (lemma-regular-graded); agent calculation of the kernel in each degree of the quotient map

proof.text: Every element of $G$ is a finite sum of its homogeneous components; since $\phi$ preserves degrees, its kernel is the direct sum of the kernels in step 4. Multiplication by the homogeneous element $F$ likewise respects the shifted degrees, so those kernels form exactly the ideal $(F)$. Define $G/(F)\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}B$ by $[g]\mapsto\phi(g)$. Surjectivity of $\phi$ gives surjectivity, and its computed kernel gives injectivity; this is the required graded $k$-algebra isomorphism. In degree one the quotient is $G_1/kF$ when $e=1$, with $F\ne0$, and is $G_1$ when $e\ge2$. Extend the nonzero vector $F$ to a basis when $e=1$; deleting it leaves $d-1$ basis vectors. When $e\ge2$ retain all $d$ basis vectors. Since the degree-one part on the right is $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$, its dimensions are as asserted.

source.place: Tag 00NO (lemma-regular-graded); elementary graded-quotient and degree-one calculation

proof.text: By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], $A$ is a domain. Since $f\ne0$, multiplication by $f$ is injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] to the Noetherian local ring $A$ and $f\in\mathfrak m$ to get $\dim B+1=d$, hence $d\ge1$ and $\dim B=d-1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], $B$ is nonzero local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, and its residue field is $k$: the map $A/\mathfrak m\to B/\mathfrak n$ sends the class of $a$ to that of $\pi(a)$ and has the inverse obtained by lifting $\pi(a)$ to $a$. The quotient map is surjective, so [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] shows that $B$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00NP (lemma-regular-domain); Tag 00KW (lemma-one-equation); elementary residue-field quotient identification

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] to the Noetherian local ring $B$: it is regular exactly when $\dim_k\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2=\dim B$. Steps 5 and 6 make this equality equivalent to $e=1$. Since $f\in\mathfrak m$ and $e$ is its unique finite order, $e=1$ is equivalent to $f\notin\mathfrak m^2$. This proves the final equivalence.
